summary: Fulham Osteopaths has 441 five-star reviews and a beautiful niche: babies and pregnancy. But nearby, another osteopathic clinic is open 7am to 9pm every day of the week, and parents searching in the evening find them first.

you.notes: Online booking (Jane); baby and pregnancy osteopathy; closed Sundays

visibility: In our searches your own website did not appear, even for your exact name and address; directories and your booking page did. For "baby osteopath Fulham", directory pages for other paediatric osteopaths came first.
lead: 441 five-star reviews: the most of any osteopath nearby.

gaps.title: Parents can't see your specialism
gaps.detail: When we searched 'baby osteopath Fulham', other paediatric osteopaths and directories came first. Your booking page appeared, but nothing that explains your baby and pregnancy care to a worried parent.

gaps.title: Directories show different hours
gaps.detail: One directory lists 9am–7:30pm with a late Wednesday; Google shows 8am–7pm. Conflicting hours make new patients hesitate.

gaps.title: Families could stay for years
gaps.detail: Mum, baby and later the whole family: automatic follow-ups after birth would keep them with you.

search.result: Your own website did not appear. The results were Fresha, WhatClinic, Doctify, the council directory and the osteopathy register. One directory lists your hours as 9am–7:30pm (Wednesday 8:30am–8:30pm), different from Google.
search.meaning: People who already know your name land on directories with inconsistent hours.

search.result: Results were led by directory pages for other paediatric osteopaths (Marble Arch, Bow) and a Mumsnet thread. Your online booking page appeared, but no page explaining your baby and pregnancy care.
search.meaning: Parents searching for exactly what you are best at don't find a page that tells them you do it.

headline.title: We searched your exact name and address. Your website appeared in none of the 16 results.
headline.detail: For "baby osteopath Fulham", the top results were directory pages for other paediatric osteopaths, not you.

scenario: It's 11pm and a new mum's three-week-old won't settle or feed on one side. A friend mentioned 'an osteopath for babies' and she searches "baby osteopath Fulham". She finds directory pages for clinics in Marble Arch and Bow, and a Mumsnet thread. Nothing tells her that the gentlest baby osteopaths in Fulham are a ten-minute walk away. She books whoever she finds first.
nochange: Your specialism stays hidden behind directories, and parents keep choosing whoever they can find at night. The families who would have come to you for years, mum, baby and later the whole family, start with someone else.
